fields.lead: Incretin-based multi-agonist drugs are reshaping how obesity and type 2 diabetes are defined and treated, while the field debates long-term use, organ-protection effects beyond glucose, and whether obesity is a disease in its own right.

papers.title: From the Triumvirate to the Ominous Octet: A New Paradigm for the Treatment of Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
papers.why: DeFronzo's Banting Lecture recast type 2 diabetes as failure across eight organs, not just insulin resistance plus a tired pancreas. It pushed treatment toward combination therapy aimed at the gut, kidney and brain as well as the islet, and it is still the map most clinicians use for why GLP-1 and SGLT2 drugs work.

papers.title: Mechanisms for Insulin Resistance: Common Threads and Missing Links
papers.why: This review set out the lipid (diacylglycerol/PKC-epsilon) account of how fat in liver and muscle blocks insulin signalling. It remains the leading mechanistic model and the main thing rival explanations, such as inflammation and mitochondrial theories, are argued against.

papers.title: What We Talk About When We Talk About Fat
papers.why: A synthesis of adipose biology that treats fat as an endocrine organ with distinct white, brown and beige cell types. It frames current work on where fat is stored, why some obesity is metabolically healthy, and whether thermogenic fat can be harnessed.

papers.title: The Incretin System: Glucagon-like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 Inhibitors in Type 2 Diabetes
papers.why: The standard account of incretin biology at the moment the first GLP-1 drugs reached patients. Everything since, from semaglutide to multi-agonists, builds on the physiology laid out here.

papers.title: Liraglutide and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes
papers.why: LEADER showed a GLP-1 agonist cut cardiovascular death, not just glucose. It turned diabetes drugs from glucose-lowering agents into organ-protection drugs and set the outcome-trial template the field now uses.

papers.title: Primary Care-Led Weight Management for Remission of Type 2 Diabetes (DiRECT): An Open-Label, Cluster-Randomised Trial
papers.why: DiRECT showed that roughly half of people with recent type 2 diabetes could reach remission through intensive weight loss in ordinary primary care. It made remission a realistic treatment goal and underpins the argument that the disease is driven by excess fat in liver and pancreas.

papers.title: Tirzepatide versus Semaglutide Once Weekly in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes
papers.why: A dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist beat the best GLP-1 drug head-to-head on both glucose and weight. It reopened the question of what GIP actually does, since GIP agonism and antagonism both seem to help, and launched the multi-agonist era.

papers.title: Triple-Hormone-Receptor Agonist Retatrutide for Obesity: A Phase 2 Trial
papers.why: Adding glucagon receptor agonism produced weight loss near 24% at 48 weeks, close to bariatric surgery. It marks the frontier of incretin pharmacology and raises the open question of how far drug-induced weight loss can and should go.

papers.title: Effects of Semaglutide on Chronic Kidney Disease in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes
papers.why: FLOW was stopped early because semaglutide clearly protected the kidneys. It is a key piece of evidence that GLP-1 drugs act across organs, which drives the current push to test them in kidney, liver, heart failure and other conditions.

papers.title: Definition and Diagnostic Criteria of Clinical Obesity
papers.why: The Lancet Commission proposed separating 'clinical obesity', a disease defined by organ dysfunction, from 'preclinical obesity' and from BMI alone. It is the field's live argument over whether obesity is a disease and who should get the new drugs.

more.title: 10-Year Follow-up of Intensive Glucose Control in Type 2 Diabetes
more.why: The UKPDS follow-up showed that early tight glucose control had a 'legacy effect' on heart attacks and death that appeared years after the trial. It is still the main evidence for treating hard early in the disease.

more.authors: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes Study Group (ACCORD)
more.title: Effects of Intensive Glucose Lowering in Type 2 Diabetes
more.why: Pushing HbA1c very low in long-standing diabetes increased deaths. Together with UKPDS it defines the timing debate and explains why guidelines individualise glucose targets.

more.title: Reduction in the Incidence of Type 2 Diabetes with Lifestyle Intervention or Metformin
more.why: Lifestyle change cut progression to diabetes by 58%, beating metformin. It remains the benchmark every prevention programme and every drug prevention trial is measured against.

more.title: Novel Subgroups of Adult-Onset Diabetes and Their Association with Outcomes: A Data-Driven Cluster Analysis of Six Variables
more.why: Clustering split adult diabetes into five subtypes with different complication risks. It started the precision-diabetes programme, which is still debating whether discrete clusters or continuous traits are the better description.

more.title: Identification and Importance of Brown Adipose Tissue in Adult Humans
more.why: This study showed that adults keep active brown fat, previously thought to vanish after infancy. It opened the thermogenic-fat research programme that is still testing whether brown and beige fat can be used against obesity.

more.title: Weight Regain and Cardiometabolic Effects After Withdrawal of Semaglutide: The STEP 1 Trial Extension
more.why: After stopping semaglutide, participants regained about two-thirds of the weight they lost within a year. It is central to the current debate about whether obesity drugs must be taken for life.

more.title: An Anti-CD3 Antibody, Teplizumab, in Relatives at Risk for Type 1 Diabetes
more.why: Teplizumab delayed the onset of type 1 diabetes by about two years, the first immune therapy to do so. It led to the first approved disease-modifying drug for type 1 diabetes and to screening for the disease before symptoms.

more.title: Romosozumab or Alendronate for Fracture Prevention in Women with Osteoporosis
more.why: Sclerostin blockade with romosozumab cut fractures more than alendronate but showed a cardiovascular signal. It defines the 'anabolic first' strategy in osteoporosis and the safety trade-off that still limits its use.

more.title: Thyroid Hormone Therapy for Older Adults with Subclinical Hypothyroidism
more.why: Levothyroxine gave no benefit to older adults with subclinical hypothyroidism. It drives the current push against overtreating mild thyroid test abnormalities, one of the most common prescriptions in medicine.

more.title: A Phase 3, Randomized, Controlled Trial of Resmetirom in NASH with Liver Fibrosis
more.why: A liver-targeted thyroid hormone receptor-beta agonist resolved steatohepatitis and improved fibrosis, leading to the first approved drug for the condition. It puts fatty liver disease at the centre of metabolic medicine alongside diabetes and obesity.

fields.lead: Neurology is shifting to biology-defined disease and targeted therapy: anti-amyloid antibodies and blood biomarkers in Alzheimer's, seed assays in Parkinson's, antisense drugs in ALS, wider thrombectomy in stroke, and implanted brain-computer interfaces.

papers.authors: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke rt-PA Stroke Study Group
papers.title: Tissue Plasminogen Activator for Acute Ischemic Stroke
papers.why: The first trial to show that a clot-busting drug given within three hours improves stroke outcomes. It created emergency stroke care as a system, and today's trials of tenecteplase and of wider time windows still build on its design.

papers.title: Endovascular Thrombectomy After Large-Vessel Ischaemic Stroke: A Meta-Analysis of Individual Patient Data from Five Randomised Trials
papers.why: Pooling the five 2015 trials showed that mechanically removing the clot roughly halves disability, with one patient helped for every 2.6 treated. It made thrombectomy standard care and is the reference for every later question about who should get it.

papers.title: Thrombectomy 6 to 24 Hours after Stroke with a Mismatch between Deficit and Infarct
papers.why: DAWN extended thrombectomy to 24 hours for patients selected by imaging. It shifted stroke care from 'time is brain' to 'tissue is brain', and today's trials are still pushing that selection logic.

papers.title: NIA-AA Research Framework: Toward a Biological Definition of Alzheimer's Disease
papers.why: This framework defined Alzheimer's by amyloid, tau and neurodegeneration biomarkers rather than symptoms. It is the foundation of current trials and diagnosis, and it remains contested because it labels symptom-free people as having the disease.

papers.title: Discriminative Accuracy of Plasma Phospho-tau217 for Alzheimer Disease vs Other Neurodegenerative Disorders
papers.why: A blood test for p-tau217 matched PET and spinal-fluid measures in identifying Alzheimer's pathology. Blood biomarkers are now moving into clinics and trial screening, which changes who can be diagnosed and how early.

papers.title: Lecanemab in Early Alzheimer's Disease
papers.why: Lecanemab cleared amyloid and slowed decline by 27% over 18 months, the first clean phase 3 win for the amyloid hypothesis. It drives the current debate over whether that effect is clinically meaningful given the risk of brain swelling and bleeding (ARIA).

papers.title: Donanemab in Early Symptomatic Alzheimer Disease: The TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 Randomized Clinical Trial
papers.why: Donanemab slowed decline, worked best in people with low tau, and let patients stop treatment once amyloid was cleared. It sharpened the case for treating early and the argument over how much benefit justifies ARIA risk and cost.

papers.title: Assessment of Heterogeneity Among Participants in the Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative Cohort Using α-Synuclein Seed Amplification: A Cross-Sectional Study
papers.why: The spinal-fluid seed amplification assay detected misfolded alpha-synuclein in about 88% of Parkinson's patients and in people before symptoms. It underpins the current proposals to define Parkinson's biologically, as Alzheimer's has been.

papers.title: Longitudinal Analysis Reveals High Prevalence of Epstein-Barr Virus Associated with Multiple Sclerosis
papers.why: Following ten million military personnel, the study found that EBV infection raised MS risk 32-fold and came before the disease. It made EBV the leading candidate cause of MS and launched vaccine and antiviral strategies.

papers.title: Trial of Antisense Oligonucleotide Tofersen for SOD1 ALS
papers.why: Tofersen lowered SOD1 protein and neurofilament levels but missed its primary endpoint, yet it was approved on the biomarker. It is the test case for gene-targeted therapy in neurodegeneration and for using neurofilament as evidence that a drug works.

more.title: Thrombectomy for Stroke at 6 to 16 Hours with Selection by Perfusion Imaging
more.why: Alongside DAWN, DEFUSE 3 showed that perfusion imaging can find salvageable brain late after onset. Its selection approach is still used and still argued over as trials test simpler imaging.

more.title: Trial of Endovascular Thrombectomy for Large Ischemic Strokes
more.why: Thrombectomy helped even patients with large established infarcts, who had been excluded from earlier trials. With related trials it is rapidly widening who qualifies for the procedure.

more.title: Two Randomized Phase 3 Studies of Aducanumab in Early Alzheimer's Disease
more.venue: The Journal of Prevention of Alzheimer's Disease
more.why: Two identical trials gave conflicting results, yet aducanumab won accelerated approval in 2021. The episode remains the field's cautionary tale about post-hoc analyses, surrogate endpoints and regulatory standards.

more.title: Revised Criteria for Diagnosis and Staging of Alzheimer's Disease: Alzheimer's Association Workgroup
more.why: The revision lets a single core biomarker, including a blood test, define Alzheimer's disease. It is the current focus of the debate over diagnosing people without symptoms.

more.title: Dementia Prevention, Intervention, and Care: 2024 Report of the Lancet Standing Commission
more.why: The Commission estimated that about 45% of dementia is linked to 14 modifiable risk factors. It anchors the prevention side of dementia research, though the estimate rests largely on observational data.

more.title: Expanded GGGGCC Hexanucleotide Repeat in Noncoding Region of C9ORF72 Causes Chromosome 9p-Linked FTD and ALS
more.why: This paper found the most common genetic cause of ALS and frontotemporal dementia, linking the two diseases. C9ORF72 biology and antisense programmes aimed at it remain a main line of ALS research.

more.title: Ocrelizumab versus Interferon Beta-1a in Relapsing Multiple Sclerosis
more.why: Depleting B cells with an anti-CD20 antibody cut relapses well beyond the standard therapy. It shifted MS from a T-cell to a B-cell disease model, which fits the EBV link and shapes current treatment.

more.title: Trial of Cannabidiol for Drug-Resistant Seizures in the Dravet Syndrome
more.why: Cannabidiol reduced convulsive seizures in a severe genetic epilepsy, leading to the first approved cannabis-derived drug. It is a reference point for treating drug-resistant epilepsy and for how much rigorous evidence supports cannabis medicine.

more.title: A High-Performance Speech Neuroprosthesis
more.why: An intracortical implant decoded attempted speech at about 62 words per minute in a person with ALS. It showed that brain-computer interfaces could restore conversation, the goal now driving the field.

more.title: An Accurate and Rapidly Calibrating Speech Neuroprosthesis
more.why: A speech brain-computer interface reached about 97% accuracy and was used daily at home by a man with ALS. It moved speech neuroprostheses from lab demonstration toward long-term clinical use.

fields.lead: Nutrition science is trying to move from confounded observational associations to controlled feeding and large randomised trials, with ultra-processed food, carbohydrate-versus-calorie models of obesity, sodium and the microbiome as the main live disputes.

papers.title: Effects on Blood Pressure of Reduced Dietary Sodium and the Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension (DASH) Diet
papers.why: A controlled feeding trial showed that the DASH diet and lower sodium each lowered blood pressure, and did so more together. It is still the strongest feeding-trial evidence behind sodium and dietary-pattern guidelines.

papers.title: Primary Prevention of Cardiovascular Disease with a Mediterranean Diet Supplemented with Extra-Virgin Olive Oil or Nuts
papers.why: The largest diet RCT for hard cardiovascular outcomes was retracted in 2018 and republished after randomisation problems were found at some sites. The reanalysis still found about 30% fewer cardiovascular events, but critics argue the flaws mean it is no longer a clean randomised trial.
papers.note: This is the 2018 republication; the original 2013 paper was retracted.

papers.title: Is Everything We Eat Associated with Cancer? A Systematic Cookbook Review
papers.venue: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
papers.why: Most common cookbook ingredients had published links to cancer risk in both directions, mostly with weak evidence. It became the standard illustration of how nutritional epidemiology produces noisy, implausible associations.

papers.title: The Challenge of Reforming Nutritional Epidemiologic Research
papers.why: Ioannidis argued that the field's observational methods, built on food questionnaires, are too confounded and imprecise to support most of its claims. It made the methods debate explicit; defenders such as Willett and Hu argue that cohort findings have often been confirmed by trials.

papers.title: Ultra-Processed Foods: What They Are and How to Identify Them
papers.why: This paper set out the NOVA classification of ultra-processed foods. The concept now drives a major research and policy agenda, while critics argue that the category is too broad and inconsistently applied to pin down any mechanism.

papers.title: Ultra-Processed Diets Cause Excess Calorie Intake and Weight Gain: An Inpatient Randomized Controlled Trial of Ad Libitum Food Intake
papers.why: In a metabolic ward, people ate about 500 extra calories a day and gained weight on an ultra-processed diet matched for presented nutrients. It is the main causal evidence for ultra-processed food harms, though it was small (20 people) and short (two weeks), and replication trials are under way.

papers.title: Effect of Low-Fat vs Low-Carbohydrate Diet on 12-Month Weight Loss in Overweight Adults and the Association With Genotype or Insulin Secretion
papers.why: Low-fat and low-carbohydrate diets produced the same weight loss, and neither genotype nor insulin secretion predicted who did better. It weakened both the diet wars and early claims for personalised diets.

papers.title: The Carbohydrate-Insulin Model of Obesity: Beyond 'Calories In, Calories Out'
papers.why: This is the clearest statement of the view that high-glycaemic carbohydrates cause obesity through insulin-driven fat storage. It is one side of a still-unresolved dispute; Hall's feeding studies are the main evidence against it.

papers.title: Personalized Nutrition by Prediction of Glycemic Responses
papers.why: Blood glucose responses to the same foods varied widely between people, and gut microbiome data helped predict them. It launched microbiome-based personalised nutrition, whose clinical benefit is still unproven.

papers.title: Effect of Salt Substitution on Cardiovascular Events and Death
papers.why: In rural China, replacing salt with a potassium-enriched substitute cut strokes, cardiovascular events and deaths. It is the strongest hard-outcome RCT for lowering sodium and raising potassium, and it counters cohort data that suggest a J-curve.

more.title: Nutritional Epidemiology (3rd ed.)
more.why: The standard textbook for the food-questionnaire and cohort methods behind most dietary guidelines. It is the methodological position the current reform debate is arguing with.

more.title: Dietary Sugars and Body Weight: Systematic Review and Meta-Analyses of Randomised Controlled Trials and Cohort Studies
more.why: Sugar affected body weight mainly through extra calories, since swapping sugar for other carbohydrates changed little. It underlies WHO's sugar guideline and keeps the debate over whether sugar is uniquely harmful.

more.title: Associations of Urinary Sodium Excretion with Cardiovascular Events in Individuals with and without Hypertension: A Pooled Analysis of Data from Four Studies
more.why: This pooled analysis reported a J-curve in which low sodium intake was also linked to more cardiovascular events. It is the main challenge to population sodium reduction and is heavily criticised for relying on spot urine samples and reverse causation.

more.title: Effect of a Plant-Based, Low-Fat Diet versus an Animal-Based, Ketogenic Diet on Ad Libitum Energy Intake
more.why: People ate about 700 fewer calories a day on a low-fat diet than on a ketogenic diet, despite higher insulin. This contradicts a key prediction of the carbohydrate-insulin model, though supporters dispute the short time frame.

more.title: Effects of a Low Carbohydrate Diet on Energy Expenditure During Weight Loss Maintenance: Randomized Trial
more.why: A low-carbohydrate diet appeared to raise energy expenditure by about 200 kcal a day during weight maintenance. It is the main trial evidence for the carbohydrate-insulin model, and Hall and others have disputed its analysis.

more.title: Diet Rapidly and Reproducibly Alters the Human Gut Microbiome
more.why: Switching between plant-based and animal-based diets reshaped the gut microbiome within days. It established diet as a fast lever on the microbiome, the starting point for diet-microbiome-health research.

more.title: Artificial Sweeteners Induce Glucose Intolerance by Altering the Gut Microbiota
more.why: Non-caloric sweeteners impaired glucose tolerance in mice and some people, through the microbiome. It kept the safety of sweeteners an open question; human results have been mixed and remain debated.

more.title: Unprocessed Red Meat and Processed Meat Consumption: Dietary Guideline Recommendations From the NutriRECS Consortium
more.why: Applying GRADE, the panel concluded that the evidence was too weak to tell most adults to cut red meat. It caused a major row over how evidence rules built for drugs should apply to nutrition.

more.title: Food in the Anthropocene: The EAT-Lancet Commission on Healthy Diets from Sustainable Food Systems
more.why: The Commission proposed a mostly plant-based 'planetary health diet' meant to serve both health and sustainability. It shapes policy and is contested on nutrient adequacy, cost and the strength of its health evidence.

more.title: A Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis and Meta-Regression of the Effect of Protein Supplementation on Resistance Training-Induced Gains in Muscle Mass and Strength in Healthy Adults
more.why: Extra protein added modestly to muscle gains from resistance training, with benefits levelling off at about 1.6 g/kg/day. It is the reference for current protein recommendations above the official RDA, a target still being argued about, especially for older adults.
